newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: ASEAN ministers say new members meet criteria.
newsitem.headline: ASEAN ministers say new members meet criteria.

text.p: Foreign ministers of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) on Friday shrugged off international pressure to defer membership for Burma, saying the three new members were ready to join.

"We believe that not only Myanmar (Burma), but also Cambodia and Laos do fulfill the criteria applicable here -- ASEAN's criteria for a new member," Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas said after arriving in Kuala Lumpur.
"We in Indonesia are prepared to have them as soon as possible," Alatas said. "But whether it'll be in July or the end of the year, I can't say for sure."

ASEAN decided last year to give membership to the three countries some time in 1997. On Saturday, the foreign ministers from Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam will decide exactly when that will happen.
A senior Burmese government spokesman told Reuters on Friday it was confident ASEAN would not be swayed by outside interference when it made its decision.

"Myanmar (Burma) is confident that the ASEAN member countries will collectively decide on what is good for the region as a whole...will decide on the future of the region on their own wisdom without giving in to outside interference," the spokesman said.

The United States has asked ASEAN to delay Burma's entry because of the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council's (SLORC) poor human rights record and suppression of the opposition led by pro-democracy leader Aung San Suu Kyi.

ASEAN nations have objected to what they see as Washington's interference in its affairs. Malaysia, this year's chairman, has been pressing for the induction to take place at ASEAN's annual meeting on July 24-25. The admission ceremony is tentatively on the schedule then.
Alternatively, the group could decide to induct the three at a December summit in Malaysia or some time in between.
"We are very flexible on the timing," said Philippine Foreign Affairs Secretary Domingo Siazon after his arrival.
"What is important is to listen to our other colleagues because they may have more information. Thailand and Vietnam are much closer neighbours (to the three)," he said.
Thai Foreign Minister Prachuab Chaiysan said ASEAN was not bothered about outside pressure, which has also come from the European Union.
"We do not feel any pressure at the moment," Prachuab said.
"The ASEAN principle is we will not attach the internal problems of its member countries into consideration (when making a decision)," he said.

Some diplomats have said that political strife in Cambodia, which has prevented the legislature from passing critical enabling legislation for membership, could end up delaying membership for all three countries. But Cambodia's ambassador to Thailand Roland Eng, who is to brief Saturday's meeting on the political situation in Cambodia, said Phnom Penh was determined to see the process through.
"Any crisis is temporary but membership is for life," Eng told reporters.
"The parties in the (Cambodian) coalition have agreed to be part of ASEAN. Since we signed the treaty, we've been preparing ourselves very hard, I can assure you," he added.
In Rangoon, a Burmese official said on Friday the government would bar entry to Aung San Suu Kyi's home and blockade her party's headquarters until after the ASEAN talks.
He said the government wanted to avoid clashes with members of her National League for Democracy (NLD), which has urged ASEAN not to admit Burma.
"They know that the NLD is planning to make some move during the ASEAN meeting, so they are banning people from access to the NLD to deter them from gathering," the source said.

Malaysia has been keen to have the three new members join at the July meeting so it could unveil a new ASEAN logo during the group's 30th anniversary celebrations. The logo features 10 rice stalks joined together, representing the 10 members.
ASEAN was founded in 1967 at the height of the Vietnam War as an anti-Communist bulwark in the region.
